name: Street Custom 'Rooftop Express' Zipline Deployment Kit
product_name: Street Custom 'Rooftop Express' Zipline Deployment Kit
description: A portable zipline system consisting of a high-strength cable, pneumatic anchor launcher, and friction-brake trolley that enables rapid transit between buildings across open gaps. The kit fires a cable anchor to a target point up to 100 meters away, tensions the cable with an integrated winch, and provides a trolley handle with variable-friction brake for speed control during the crossing. The system is designed for one-way transit — ascending ziplines are possible but require motorized trolleys that add weight and complexity. Street operators use it for rapid building-to-building movement, escape routes, and tactical repositioning in urban environments.
legality: Legal as equipment — illegal when used for unauthorized building access

specifications.info: accurate to 1-meter at 50 meters; anchor is expendable
specifications.setup time: 90 seconds from anchor launch to crossing

story_hooks: A series of Tier 2 rooftop burglaries are connected by zipline anchor marks on building parapets — someone is running a route across the skyline, hitting targets along a planned path.
An emergency evacuation from a burning building was facilitated by a Rooftop Express kit — the operator ziplined 40 people to an adjacent building before fire services arrived.
related_entities: Ringo Corponation SlipThread MX-3 Urban Cable Micro-Mobility Rig

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, modular mobility system resembling a compressed mountaineering kit meets industrial pneumatic tool. The anchor launcher dominates—a stubby, reinforced cylinder with a flared muzzle. The trolley is a minimalist T-bar handle with integrated brake lever and LED status strip. Cable spools onto a compact reel secured to a carbon-fiber carrying frame.
physical_description.dimensions: Anchor launcher 25cm long, trolley handle 30cm span, reel unit 40cm × 20cm × 15cm. Total kit forms a backpack-sized bundle when deployed case closed.
physical_description.weight_description: 3.5 kg total—handheld and shoulder-carry capable. Trolley alone is pocketable; cable reel requires backpack mounting or dual-carry straps.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum chassis, reinforced polymer grip panels, braided steel cable (100m), titanium anchor head
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal with satin anodize on launcher. Textured rubberized grip surfaces. Cable has protective nylon sleeve in sections prone to UV damage.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal-gray primary body with neon cyan accent striping on trolley brake lever and status indicators. Anchor head in brushed steel. Cable sheathing dark navy.
physical_description.interface_elements: Pneumatic pressurization valve with analog gauge (0–15 bar), trigger-style anchor release, ergonomic brake lever with friction-resistance detents (3 settings), LED status array (power, tension, anchor lock, overload warning), quick-release cable connector with safety latch, winch engagement button
distinctive_features: Pneumatic launcher muzzle flares outward like a miniature artillery piece
Trolley handle splits into asymmetric grips for one-handed operation while braking
Integrated tension readout via mechanical dial on reel unit
Anchor impacts generate auto-lock confirmation—visible electromagnetic clamp closing on tether spool
Brake lever features haptic feedback detents, audible click at each friction level
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Street Custom logo (stylized SC in angular font) embossed on reel housing. Regulatory stamps: GLMZ Load Certification (120kg), Pneumatic Safety Standard φ-8847, serial number laser-etched on launcher. Faded warning decals in Mandarin, Spanish, and English on pressure valve.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained units show cable wear at anchor end and brake dust on trolley wheels. Field-used kits display impact scars on reel housing, patched cable sections, and faded logo from UV exposure. Pressure gauge often reads slightly below recommended (indicating slow seal wear common in used units).
